## CEO overview

What is changing: Firstmate now gives workers a safe, supported way to recover a branch after a no-mistakes validation run ends while the validation pipeline still owns it.
  The worker can adopt the preserved pipeline result only when structured status explicitly offers custody recovery, and otherwise receives a concrete refusal instead of being pushed toward hand-edited history.
Why it matters: A failed or cancelled validation must not strand otherwise recoverable work or force a worker to guess whether a reset, rebase, or other history rewrite is safe.
Customer or business impact: Future Firstmate tasks can resume from preserved validation work without losing unlanded captain changes, while ambiguous or unsupported states remain visible for firstmate intervention.
Risk and rollout: Low.
  The new helper performs a read-only structured status check, requires a clean branch before recovery, and delegates the only branch mutation to no-mistakes' guarded `axi sync --recover` command.
  Dirty worktrees, failed status reads, user-owned branches, and unsupported custody actions do not change files or refs.
  The behavior is inert until a worker explicitly uses the helper after a terminal validation outcome.

## What changed technically

- Added `bin/fm-nm-recover.sh`, which reads `branch_sync.next_action.code` from the current structured `no-mistakes axi status` response and invokes `no-mistakes axi sync --recover` only for the exact `recover_custody` offer.
- Made dirty, detached, failed-status, missing-action, and unsupported-action paths explicit refusals that preserve the branch and identify the next read-only step; an already `user_owned` branch is a safe no-op.
- Updated the generated no-mistakes worker brief and `AGENTS.md` section 7 to require custody reconciliation after every failed or cancelled run before follow-up commits or a fresh run.
- Added an archived stuck-custody status fixture and executable regressions proving guarded recovery selection, unlanded-work preservation, unsupported-state refusal, and user-owned handling.
- Added `.github/pr-bodies/24.md` so this pull request's required communication narrative is reviewable in the branch itself.

## Validation

Checks passed: The focused recovery and brief suites pass, including the archived terminal custody fixture and dirty-worktree preservation case.
  The full ShellCheck and actionlint lint path passes with the pinned tools, and the documentation ownership check passes.
  No-mistakes review applied one safety fix requiring failed structured status reads to be rejected before interpreting custody state.
  Hosted `pr-communication` and `verify-source-of-truth` checks pass after the live description was updated with this narrative while retaining the machine-owned Pipeline section.
Checks not run: Hosted checks have not run against the follow-up commit that adds this tracked narrative.
Evidence and limitations: The reproduction uses an archived failed-run status whose `branch_sync.next_action.code` is `recover_custody`, and the executable test drives the real Firstmate helper against that serialized public status with an isolated command transport.
  The helper intentionally refuses when status cannot prove the recovery transition or when the worktree contains unlanded changes; those cases remain firstmate decisions rather than automatic history operations.
  The hosted communication passes prove the narrative contract on the prior target SHA; the outer executor remains responsible for final-head hosted checks.

## Module-boundary decision

Module-boundary decision: Current modules retained.
  The helper is a narrow Firstmate entrypoint around no-mistakes' existing guarded branch synchronization and does not duplicate its custody or history rules.
  Structured status parsing and safety refusal stay at the worker boundary, while no-mistakes remains the sole owner of branch mutation.

## Decision needed

No product decision is required for this change.
  The captain retains merge authority, and this pull request must not be merged automatically.
